title: docs(#6651): Proxy bucket triage — three recorded causes corrected, and the measurement lane was wrong
author: claude
head: 98bd516d49e26065a8c30310b0d622273d23d484
body:
## Description

Docs only. No source change, no conformance claim, no delta.

ES2015 on `--target standalone` measures 10,933/11,704 = 93%, and the gap is concentrated rather than scattered. `Proxy` is the largest concentrated deficit outside cross-realm: 115 fail + 3 CE of 431 rows. This PR is the triage of that bucket — a partition by actual cause, so the next lane can size the work instead of rediscovering it.

The headline is that **the bucket does not partition the way this repo's own notes record it.** Every recorded cause was re-probed and three are wrong, including the two largest by row count.

## The partition

Reproduced from the per-row standalone JSONL intersected with `generate-editions.ts`'s own `parseFrontmatter` / `classifyEdition` / `--host-free` pass definition, so it matches the published artifact exactly.

**Host vs standalone: 59 host-pass (a genuine standalone gap) / 59 host-fail (shared front-end, a different slice). Exactly half.**

| group | rows | standalone-only | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Function.prototype` members unreadable as values | 7 (+3 later editions, +1 CE) | 7 | root-caused and sited, unfixed |
| proxy in a prototype chain is invisible | 15 | 6 | architectural, confirmed |
| cross-realm | 10 | 5 | belongs to the cross-realm slice |
| revoked-proxy reachability | 8 | 6 | grouped, **not** root-caused |
| ownKeys / gOPN invariants | 7 | 6 | grouped, **not** root-caused |
| ArraySpeciesCreate through a proxy | 5 | 0 | shared front-end |
| residual, individually sited | ~66 | 29 | mixed |

The last three rows of that table are **directory-shaped labels, not causes** — which is exactly the defect that produced the corrections below. They should not be used to size work without re-probing.

## Three recorded causes corrected

1. **"nested proxy forwarding (`target-is-proxy`) is broken" — wrong.** Nested trap-absent forwarding works: `new Proxy(new Proxy({x:1},{get(){…}}),{})` runs the inner trap and returns its value, and the `has` twin likewise (4/4). The 24 `*-target-is-proxy.js` rows are **composites** — each also does `Object.create(proxy)` and/or reads builtin-prototype members through the proxy. Grouping by filename manufactured a 24-row cause that does not exist.
2. **"trap `this` is not the handler" — wrong.** The trap `this` *is* the handler wherever a trap runs; the direct `has`/`get`/`set` controls all pass. `_handler === undefined` fails because **the trap never runs** — it is the prototype-chain case. Not a calling-convention defect.
3. **`Proxy/has/trap-is-undefined.js` is not a Proxy row at all.** It fails on `"length" in Object.create(Array.prototype)`, which answers `false` with no proxy present. `"push" in` the same object answers `true`, so the chain walk is fine — `Array.prototype`'s own `length` is invisible to `in`.

The prototype-chain note **re-probed as correct**: a proxy in a prototype chain is *completely* invisible — `has`, `get` and `set` all skip it (`$Object.$proto` is `ref null $Object`, and `$Proxy` is not a subtype). One route the earlier notes missed: `$Object` has only **four** `struct.new` sites, so adding a `protoExtern: externref` field is mechanically tractable and is *not* the non-final/subtype change that broke #2009. Not attempted — it rewrites every proto-walk loop plus `Object.create` / `setPrototypeOf` / `instanceof` / `isPrototypeOf`. That wants an architect spec.

## The largest landable cause, sited but not taken

**No `Function.prototype` member is readable as a value off a function object in standalone.** `f.apply`, `f.call`, `f.bind`, `f.toString` — including computed-key and laundered-receiver spellings — all evaluate to `undefined` (7/7). Calls are unaffected; only the value read.

That is the whole `built-ins/Function/prototype/toString/proxy-*` bucket: 10 fail + 1 CE measured authoritatively, 7 of them ES2015, all 7 host-pass. The chain: the harness's `assertNativeFunction` uses `"" + fn`; each row then does `…(new Proxy(<callable>,{apply(){}})).apply`. With the real harness prepended at module top level, line 1 passes (already served by #5269's `buildProxyCallableToStringArm`) and line 2 fails with `"undefined"` — its operand is `proxy.apply`.

Site: `src/codegen/closure-props.ts`, the `__closure_prop_get` terminal miss (`protoIndexRecvGetMissInstrs(ctx, 0, 1) ?? getMiss()`, ~L978). That consult does route a closure receiver to the Function brand companion, but the companion is minted empty — `native-proto.ts` says so outright, and `ensureFunctionNativeProtoGlue` is reached only from syntactic sites. Naming `Function.prototype` in source does not fix the closure read; that spelling is a separate fold, which is why the gap is invisible from it.

**A warning for whoever takes it.** A static fold in `property-access.ts` mirroring `tryCompileStandaloneFunctionHasInstanceRead` would also move all 10 rows, and is tempting because `new Proxy(f,h)` carries `f`'s TS type so `fact.kind === "function"` holds. Do not take it: it bypasses a `get` trap on the handler, trading 10 rows for a silent MOP violation.

## A measurement correction that matters more than the rows

**Standalone *is* measurable in the CI-faithful `runTest262Chunk` lane in this container.** The previously recorded "no built runtime-eval provider" blocker did not apply; the only missing pieces were two gitignored build products (`npx esbuild scripts/{compiler,runtime}-bundle-entry.ts`, under a second each). An earlier PR in this series stated the opposite — that correction supersedes it.

Two consequences:

- **The test262 worker compiles through those bundles.** Rebuild after every `src/` edit or you measure the previous tree.
- **The ad-hoc snippet lane disagreed with the harness four times on this bucket, always in the reassuring direction.** `"" + proxyOfFunction` answers correctly when the operand has a static type, and the defect only reproduces once the value arrives via an untyped parameter *and* the assertions run at module top level. Anchor claims to `runTest262Chunk` or to a snippet with the real harness text prepended.

## Sweeps

Complete: the 118-row partition (offline, full JSONL); the `Function/prototype/toString/proxy-` authoritative sweep (11 rows, 0 pass / 10 fail / 1 CE, **0 `error` rows**); a 2-row `Proxy/has` authoritative control (2 fail, 0 `error` rows, both reproducing the baseline error text verbatim).

Not run: any before/after sweep. No source changed, so **no delta is claimed and no regression test was proven red** — there was nothing to prove red.

## Not done

`revoked-proxy` (8 rows) and `ownKeys`/`gOPN` invariants (7 rows) are grouped but not root-caused. No code change: the window went to triage, and three corrected causes are worth more than a half-proven change in the dynamic property-read path, which is hot and whose wholesale-seeding variant would move `for…in` / `hasOwnProperty` / `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` in the same step.

Gates run bare: `check-loc-budget`, `check-func-budget`, `check-coercion-sites`, `check:oracle-ratchet`, `check:dead-exports`, `check-host-import-policy` (`src/runtime.ts` untouched), `check-compiler-boundaries --mode inventory --base HEAD^1`.

#!/bin/bash
# Check that the Proxy bucket triage documentation contains the three corrected causes
# This PR corrects: 1) nested proxy forwarding, 2) trap this binding, 3) Proxy/has/trap-is-undefined.js classification

FILE="plan/issues/6651-es2015-standalone-100pct-execution-plan.md"

# Check that the file exists
if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: Documentation file not found"
    exit 1
fi

# Count occurrences of key correction markers
count=$(grep -cE "nested.*proxy.*forwarding|trap.*this.*handler|trap-is-undefined" "$FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")

if [ "$count" -ge 3 ]; then
    echo "PASS: All three documented corrections found in Proxy bucket triage"
    exit 0
else
    echo "FAIL: Missing corrections (found $count, expected at least 3)"
    exit 1
fi
